articles.title: The Gap-Strap Restroom Privacy Gap-Blocker Is The New 'Must Have' For College Students
articles.description: - Affordable, portable solution blocks intrusive gaps in restroom stalls - ST. LOUIS, Mo., Aug. 26, 2026 (SEND2PRESS NEWSWIRE) -- Restroom Privacy remains a serious concern on college campuses nationwide. Due to increased incidents of video voyeurism and trespassing, 72% of Americans worry about their privacy and safety in shared restrooms. The Gap-Strap™ from Bamsaw Industries, LLC addresses this. Whether at school, work, restaurants, airports, or entertainment venues, restroom privacy has become an issue affecting millions every day. "As a father of kids in college, I know firsthand the worries my kids and their friends have when it comes to using campus restrooms," says Bob Kodner, inventor and president of The Gap-Strap. Kodner continues, "As parents, we want our kids to feel safe when they're away from home, and for many students, it's their first time away from home." Kodner goes on to say, "It's not just college students. Two hundred million people use a public restroom every week. Most public and commercial restrooms have sizable gaps at stall doors that make users feel unsafe and exposed. Restroom privacy is more than a restroom concern - it's a personal safety concern." THE GAP-STRAP PORTABLE STALL-GAP BLOCKER IMPROVES RESTROOM PRIVACY AND SAFETY IN PUBLIC RESTROOMS The Gap-Strap, a portable stall-gap blocker, is an instant and effective solution that works in any restroom. "Public and commercial restrooms create uncomfortable experiences due to privacy-violating gaps at stall doors," Kodner explains. "The Gap-Strap eliminates the risk of strangers viewing us in a compromising position." Designed for convenience, The Gap-Strap simply unrolls and attaches to the top of restroom stalls. The Gap-Strap is pre-measured, with an ergonomically weighted design engineered to deliver instant and reliable privacy. "Best of all," Kodner adds, "The Gap-Strap provides the peace of mind we all want when using a public or commercial restroom." The Gap-Strap stall gap-blockers are made in the USA and engineered for use in all public and commercial restrooms. pendingReview.title: Tempe district investigating dance room changing area after voyeurism arrest
pendingReview.description: TEMPE, AZ (AZFamily) -- Why were teen girls changing clothes in a camera-equipped dance room instead of a locker room at an East Valley school this year? That's the question Tempe Union High School District is now trying to answer. The district has opened an internal investigation into how a dance room at Corona del Sol High School came to be used by students as a changing area. The practice came to light after a 28-year-old district employee was arrested for allegedly spying on undressed girls inside the space earlier this month. Antony N. Cruz, who worked as a surveillance officer, was booked on seven counts of voyeurism and is being held on a $100,000 cash-only bond in connection with the incident. How the dance room became a changing area District officials stressed the space is a dance room, not a locker room, and was never designated by the district or school administration as a place for students to change clothes. During recent locker room renovations, the district said it approved a request from school administration to set up separate, camera-free locations for students to change. Officials said the dance room was not one of the approved locations. A security camera was installed in the room in 2024 for campus safety purposes related to the room's exterior access, according to the district. The internal investigation is now focused on four questions: * How and why students were using the dance room to change * Whether established procedures were followed * How the room was being used * What corrective action may be necessary "We understand why families have questions, and we share their concern," the district said. "Our responsibility now is to fully understand what occurred, be transparent about what we learn, and take appropriate action." Allegations against the security guard The investigation follows accusations that Cruz gained access to camera footage showing a room of young teen girls undressing in the dance space, and never told school staff or law enforcement about it. Instead, investigators say Cruz began downloading the recordings onto a school computer in mid-July. He allegedly downloaded several videos, at least seven of which showed girls changing clothes, ranging from four minutes to two hours long. Download records showed the videos were saved to thumb drives and other storage devices, and school system data showed Cruz had accessed the footage remotely from his home on a Saturday, according to court paperwork. In an interview with police, Cruz allegedly admitted he learned about the girls changing in the first week of school and his "attention was drawn" to students removing their clothes while the room was being recorded. He reportedly said he initially felt uncomfortable and "tried" to tell someone, but he did not specify who he told or what exactly he was seeing, according to police. Court documents state Cruz told investigators he downloaded the videos to "preserve them" and saved them to his cell phone. He reportedly admitted to inappropriately touching himself while watching the footage, but said it felt "wrong" because he knew the girls were between 13 and 15 years old. Cruz was arrested at his Phoenix home on Saturday. His termination is pending school board approval. See a spelling or grammatical error in our story? Please click here to report it. pendingReview.title: Two suspects arrested for selling 14,000 private images they secretly recorded with hidden cameras at a beauty center.
pendingReview.description: An investigation has been launched in Istanbul's Bakırköy district over allegations that secretly recorded footage of customers at a beauty center was made available for a fee on social media platforms. In the operation, 7 devices containing hidden camera setups were seized, and it was determined that 14 thousand videos were published through a platform. Two suspects taken into custody were arrested and sent to prison. Two suspects were arrested regarding the allegation that images of customers at a beauty center in Bakirkoy were secretly recorded and shown for a fee on social media platforms. HIDDEN CAMERA SETUP SEIZED: THEY SOLD 14 THOUSAND VIDEOS Teams from the Bakirkoy District Police Department conducted an operation following a tip that customers' images were being secretly recorded at a beauty and epilation center operating in the district, and that these recordings were being shown for a fee on social media platforms. During a search of the workplace, 7 devices -- 1 active and 6 dismantled -- containing hidden camera setups, along with various digital materials, were seized. It was determined that 14 thousand videos had been published on a platform. 2 SUSPECTS ARRESTED The business owner and the 2 suspects who installed the camera system were taken into custody on charges of 'violation of privacy', 'unlawful acquisition of personal data', and 'obscenity'. After their procedures at the police station were completed, the suspects were referred to the courthouse and subsequently arrested and sent to prison.

pendingReview.title: Man sought after alleged voyeurism incident in Kew Gardens washroom - Beach Metro Community News
pendingReview.description: Toronto police are looking for a man in connection with an alleged voyeurism incident inside a washroom at Kew Gardens park in the Beach earlier this week. Police were called to the park on Tuesday, Aug. 25, at 4 p.m. for reports of the incident that allegedly took place in a washroom. According to police, an 11-year-old girl entered a park washroom and a man allegedly took photos of her when she was in one of the stalls. Police alleged that the man was already in the washroom when the girl entered and he took the photos through gaps in the stall. The girl sought assistance and the man fled in an unknown direction. The man is described as black, age 27 to 30, approximately five-feet, 10-inches tall with a medium/athletic build. He had a "black grown-out buzz cut style hair with tiny curls" and a short beard, police said. He was last seen wearing a black baseball cap, black-framed sunglasses, a black shirt with a white "arctic" logo, black shorts, and black running shoes. Investigators are looking to speak to anyone who was in the area around the time of the incident and that may have seen the suspect. Anyone with information is asked to contact police in 55 Division at 416-808-5500, or Crime Stoppers anonymously at 416-222-8477 or at https://www.222tips.com
